definition: a thin tube with a light and camera used to look inside the body

collocations.example: The doctor carefully inserted the endoscope through the patient's nose.
A flexible endoscope lets surgeons examine the stomach without major surgery.

definition: relating to a bishop or to a church governed by bishops

collocations.example: She was baptized in the local episcopal church last spring.
The new rules expanded episcopal authority over the parish schools.

definition: the smooth, mown part of a golf course between the tee and the green

collocations.example: Her long drive landed on the fairway near the green.
He strolled down the fairway toward his second shot.

definition: (of a young bird) to grow the feathers needed to fly

collocations.example: The young owls fledge about five weeks after hatching.
Only two chicks fledged successfully from the nest this year.

definition: to say or recite something in a slow, steady voice, often without changing pitch

collocations.example: The priest began to intone a prayer over the crowd.
The judge intoned the verdict solemnly to the silent courtroom.

definition: the small, soft, legless larva of a fly

collocations.example: Maggots quickly infested the meat left out in the heat.
The old trash can was crawling with white maggots.

definition: animal waste spread on soil to help plants grow

collocations.example: The farmer spread manure across the field before planting.
She mixed well-rotted manure into the garden soil each spring.

definition: a person who sails or navigates a ship; a sailor

collocations.example: An experienced mariner can read the weather from the clouds.
The old mariner navigated the ship safely through the storm.

definition: to treat or examine someone using the methods of psychoanalysis

collocations.example: The therapist spent months trying to psychoanalyze her anxious patient.
He has a habit of constantly psychoanalyzing his own coworkers.

definition: a rough metal tool used to file or scrape wood and other materials

collocations.example: He used a rasp to smooth the rough wooden edge.
A wood rasp quickly shapes the surface before final sanding.

definition: the mass of eggs inside a female fish, often eaten as food

collocations.example: Fish roe is considered a delicacy in many coastal cultures.
Workers harvest the roe from the fish by hand.

definition: a low silvery shrub with a strong smell that grows in dry western North America

collocations.example: The dry wind carried the sharp scent of sagebrush.
They drove for hours through open sagebrush country.

definition: a soft stuffed toy bear that children often play with

collocations.example: The toddler hugged her teddy tightly all night long.
A worn old teddy sat on the child's pillow.

definition: a small jumping animal like a frog but with rougher, drier skin

collocations.example: A fat, warty toad sat still beside the pond.
The toad hopped slowly across the damp garden path.

definition: a wrongful act, other than a breach of contract, for which someone can be sued

collocations.example: She studied tort law during her second year of law school.
A business can commit a tort by misleading its customers.

definition: a person with no home or job who travels from place to place

collocations.example: An old tramp slept under the bridge near the station.
In those torn clothes he looked just like a tramp.

definition: to transfer blood from one person into another person's body

collocations.example: Doctors had to transfuse blood after the serious accident.
Nurses must safely transfuse the patient over several hours.

definition: goods or articles of a particular kind that are made for sale

collocations.example: The museum displayed fine ware from the eighteenth century.
The store sells pots, pans, and other kitchen ware.

definition: able to be taken and used, especially for one's own benefit

collocations.example: An appropriable resource can be claimed by whoever reaches it first.
The idea was too easily appropriable to protect by patent.

definition: forming or relating to the base or lowest layer of something

collocations.example: New skin cells form in the basal layer of the epidermis.
Exercise can slightly raise your basal metabolic rate over time.

definition: a woman's male lover or boyfriend (an old-fashioned word)

collocations.example: She arrived at the party with her latest beau.
She finally introduced her beau to her strict parents.

definition: to cause constant trouble or difficulty for someone

collocations.example: Constant complaints began to beleaguer the new store manager.
The project was beleaguered by problems from the very start.

definition: to give a false impression of

collocations.example: Her lively step and bright eyes belie her true age.
His calm tone belied the fact that he was furious.

definition: to speak in a disrespectful way about God or sacred things

collocations.example: The angry crowd accused him of blaspheming against God.
No one in the quiet village dared to blaspheme openly.

definition: a golf score of one stroke more than par for a hole

collocations.example: He made a bogey on the final hole and lost.
A double bogey early in the round hurt her score.

definition: insincere talk about moral or religious matters, meant to sound good

collocations.example: Voters are tired of the politician's empty political cant.
His speech was full of cant about helping the poor.

definition: to make someone lose loyalty or satisfaction toward a group or leader

collocations.example: Harsh new taxes began to disaffect many loyal voters.
The staff grew increasingly disaffected with the new manager.

definition: an informal word for a man or guy, used especially in American English

collocations.example: That new coworker seems like a pretty cool dude.
Hey dude, can you give me a ride home?

definition: to make someone feel very happy and excited

collocations.example: The surprise victory seemed to elate the entire crowd.
She was elated by the news of her promotion.

definition: relating to the thin layer of tissue that covers body surfaces and organs

collocations.example: Epithelial cells line the inside of the small intestine.
The body works constantly to regenerate damaged epithelial tissue.

definition: a polite title placed after a person's full name, especially for a lawyer in the US

collocations.example: The formal letter was addressed to John Smith, Esquire.
The attorney chose to sign off as Esquire.

definition: an informal word for a five-dollar or five-pound note

collocations.example: Can you lend me a fiver until next payday?
He pulled a crumpled fiver from his coat pocket.

definition: a man who belongs to a Catholic religious group and often works among people

collocations.example: A Franciscan friar greeted the travelers at the gate.
The gentle friar blessed the couple before the ceremony.

definition: a small, ugly creature in stories that is mischievous or evil

collocations.example: An evil goblin guarded the gold deep under the mountain.
In the tale, a goblin lurks beneath the old bridge.

definition: a low evergreen plant with small purple or white flowers that grows on hills

collocations.example: Purple heather bloomed across the rolling Scottish hills.
Low heather covered the moor as far as we could see.

definition: a person whose beliefs are against the official teachings of a religion

collocations.example: He became known as a notorious heretic in his own time.
The scholar was condemned as a heretic by the council.

definition: the study of the microscopic structure of body tissues

collocations.example: Medical students must study histology to understand body tissues.
The histology report confirmed that the tumor was benign.

definition: a system of alternative medicine using tiny amounts of natural substances

collocations.example: Some doctors in the region still practice homeopathy today.
Her strong belief in homeopathy surprised many of her colleagues.

definition: unable to control the release of urine or waste from the body

collocations.example: After the long surgery, the elderly man became incontinent.
Nurses regularly check and change an incontinent patient.

definition: to change the form of a word to show tense, number, or case

collocations.example: In Spanish you must inflect the verb for each subject.
English nouns do not inflect for tense like verbs do.

definition: informal: having large, well-developed muscles

collocations.example: He spent a whole year in the gym to get jacked.
After months of training, her arms looked seriously jacked.

definition: a noisy, colorful bird of the crow family, often with blue feathers

collocations.example: A bright blue jay landed on the garden fence.
A jay called loudly from the top of the oak.

definition: a nobleman ranking above a count and below a duke

collocations.example: The palace once belonged to a wealthy French marquis.
The marquis hosted a grand ball at his country estate.

definition: an alcoholic drink made from fermented honey and water

collocations.example: The guests drank mead from large wooden cups.
He raised a cup of mead to the king.

definition: a tiny particle with almost no mass and no electric charge

collocations.example: It is extremely difficult to detect a single neutrino.
The huge neutrino detector sits deep beneath a mountain.

definition: relating to the philosophical study of the nature of being and existence

collocations.example: The ontological argument tries to prove God's existence through logic.
Her concern was purely ontological rather than strictly practical.

definition: a chaplain or priest, especially one serving in the armed forces

collocations.example: The soldiers trusted their kind army padre completely.
He went to speak to the padre before the battle.

definition: the scientific study of fossils and ancient life forms

collocations.example: She decided to study paleontology after visiting the fossil museum.
The paleontology professor showed us a real dinosaur bone.
